title: Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Information Retrieval

visual_explainer.question: When can corpus-aware retrieval-action compilation replace multi-round result-conditioned search?
visual_explainer.takeaway: SIRA moves control before evidence inspection: the LLM predicts missing evidence vocabulary, grounds it with corpus statistics, and compiles weighted lexical retrieval rather than learning vocabulary through repeated snippet exposure.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Multi-round search agents, generic LLM query expansion, trained dense/sparse retrievers, and ordinary BM25.

analysis.tldr: SIRA challenges the assumption that search-agent intelligence requires many retrieval rounds: it uses LLM priors plus corpus-visible document-frequency signals to compile a discriminative weighted BM25 action before reading result passages, achieving strong retrieval quality while exposing a new control point—retrieval programming rather than result-conditioned exploration.
analysis.problem: Multi-round search agents often compensate for a weak or opaque retrieval interface by reading snippets, discovering corpus vocabulary, and reformulating repeatedly. That can be expensive and confounds policy quality with information leaked by earlier retrieval rounds.
analysis.core_idea: Use a frozen LLM to predict vocabulary that relevant evidence is likely to contain, ground those proposed terms against corpus statistics such as document frequency, prune absent/over-common terms, and compile a weighted BM25 retrieval action. The main BEIR setting additionally performs expensive offline LLM enrichment of document vocabulary; BrowseComp-Wikipedia removes that step and instead uses grounded Wikipedia categories as corpus-visible structure.
analysis.agent_loop: predict expected evidence vocabulary → check corpus statistics / validate constraints → compile weighted lexical action → retrieve; in the strict BEIR setting there is no result-conditioned reformulation before the final retrieval
analysis.retrieval_design: SIRA treats the inverted index as an observable control surface: document frequency and IDF make candidate terms measurable before retrieval. Query-side expansion is filtered and weighted; corpus-side enrichment injects predicted missing terms offline in the main method. The large-scale Wikipedia setting uses category-grounded lexical controls and may issue multiple evidence-blind BM25 calls under a fixed page budget.
analysis.evidence: Across ten BEIR datasets, SIRA reports average Recall@10 0.6908 and NDCG@10 0.5723, versus E5 at 0.6478 / 0.5434, SPLADE at 0.6253 / 0.5223, Search-R1(E5) at 0.6161 / 0.5216, and BM25 at 0.5302 / 0.4247. HyDE, CoT, GrepRAG, ShellAgent, and SIRA share the same frozen Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 backbone; Search-R1 does not. On BrowseComp-Wikipedia, the strongest SIRA configuration (Claude 4.6 Opus) reports Recall@1/10/100 of 9.70/15.27/36.14 versus the Claude Perplexity agent at 2.59/4.74/32.33. A useful counterexample is backbone-specific: with GPT-5.4, SIRA reaches 5.71/13.13/18.51 while Perplexity reaches 3.02/6.90/31.47, so SIRA is worse at Recall@100 for that backbone.
analysis.why_it_matters: SIRA supplies a strong counterweight to 'more search rounds are better'. It suggests adaptivity can move upstream into corpus-aware action compilation: if the agent can observe discriminative index signals before retrieval, some exploratory rounds become unnecessary. The right comparison is therefore not one-shot versus multi-round in the abstract, but what corpus information and retrieval controls are available before the first evidence is read.
limitations: The main BEIR method uses expensive LLM corpus-side enrichment over every document; this is a substantial offline cost and is removed in the Wikipedia-scale setting.
The frozen LLM is assumed to carry useful domain vocabulary priors; transfer to domains far outside pretraining knowledge is not established.
Search-R1 is not a same-backbone/controller baseline, so some agentic comparisons are not fully controlled.
BrowseComp-Wikipedia gives SIRA grounded Wikipedia category structure while the Perplexity baseline sees a production search interface; the result mixes retrieval-interface design with search policy.
The Wikipedia setting is not literally one BM25 call: it may issue multiple evidence-blind category-grounded calls under the page budget, and GPT-5.4 SIRA loses to GPT-5.4 Perplexity at Recall@100.
